newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: INTERVIEW-OUB sees 40 pct foreign income.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-OUB sees 40 pct foreign income.

text.p: Overseas Union Bank Ltd hopes its income from non-Singaporean operations will grow to at least 40 percent of its total operations, president and chief executive officer Peter Seah said on Friday.

He said OUB, one of Singapore's four main banks with assets at the end of 1995 of Singapore $25.63 billion, was the only Singapore bank with more than 30 percent of its income derived from overseas operations.
"Our objective is to grow our overseas income hopefully over the next five years from the current 30 percent to at least 40 percent," he told Reuters in an interview.
"We have grown the percentage already from 20 percent about five years ago," Seah said.
He said OUB was purely focused in Asia.

"Our operations in Malaysia are doing extremely well, and similarly our operations in Hong Kong and China and we intend to really maximise our presence within the region, particularly in ASEAN," he said.
The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
"We are the only Singapore bank with a representation in every country in ASEAN," he added.
Seah said OUB's objective was to be a leading regional bank within the region.

"And we want to help our customers extend their business outside the region...We have a growing pool of wealthy individuals and companies within the region who want to distribute their wealth through investments worldwide."
